lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Timothy charged at Ephesus: sound teaching and the law
nodes.d: Paul left Timothy at Ephesus to charge some not to teach other doctrine or follow fables and endless genealogies; the aim of the commandment is love, and the law is good when used lawfully.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul left Timothy at Ephesus (1:3-5)?
ev: State the aim of the charge (1:5)
Explain how 1:8-11 says the law is used lawfully

nodes.d: Paul's letter to Timothy at Ephesus about sound doctrine, prayer, order in the church, qualified leaders, and a minister's conduct and charge.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what 1 Timothy is about (see 3:14-15)?
ev: Describe how 3:15 states the letter's purpose
Name the main sections: false teaching, prayer and conduct, leaders, Timothy's ministry, groups in the church, closing charge

nodes.d: Paul thanks Christ for putting him into the ministry though he was a blasphemer and persecutor; Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, and Paul charges Timothy to hold faith and a good conscience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about himself and about why Christ Jesus came into the world (1:13-16)?
ev: Recite or paraphrase 1:15
Say what Paul says his case shows about Christ (1:16)

nodes.t: Prayer for all, one God, one mediator
nodes.d: Prayer is to be made for all men, including kings; God our Saviour wills all to be saved, and there is one God and one mediator, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself a ransom for all.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what 2:5-6 teaches about Jesus as mediator?
ev: List the kinds of prayer in 2:1
State who the one mediator is (2:5)

nodes.t: Conduct in the church: men, women and teaching
nodes.d: Paul gives instruction on men praying and on women's modesty and good works, and says he does not permit a woman to teach or have authority over a man, grounding this in the order of Adam and Eve's creation and the deception.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what reasons Paul gives from Genesis in 2:13-14 for his instruction in 2:12?
ev: Describe what the text says about men praying and women adorning themselves (2:8-10)
State the reasons Paul gives in 2:13-14

nodes.d: Paul lists the character required of a bishop (overseer) and of deacons and their wives, including a well-ordered household, a good report and tested blamelessness.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list some qualities of an overseer in 3:2-7 and say why household management matters (3:5)?
ev: Name several qualifications in 3:2-7
Say how deacons are to be proved (3:10)

nodes.t: The church and the mystery of godliness
nodes.d: Paul writes so Timothy may know how to behave in the house of God, the church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth, and states the mystery of godliness: God manifest in the flesh, received up into glory.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name what Paul says about Christ in 1 Timothy 3:16?
ev: Say how 3:15 describes the church
List the six statements about Christ in 3:16

nodes.t: Departing from the faith: good creation received with thanks
nodes.d: The Spirit says some will depart from the faith, forbidding marriage and certain foods; Paul says every creature of God is good and sanctified by the word of God and prayer.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul says nothing is to be refused if received with thanksgiving (4:4-5)?
ev: State what the false teachers forbid (4:3)
Explain why 4:4-5 says food is not to be refused

nodes.t: A good minister of Jesus Christ
nodes.d: Timothy is to refuse profane fables, train himself in godliness, set an example in word, conduct, love, faith and purity, devote himself to reading, exhortation and doctrine, and not neglect his gift.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul tells Timothy to do so that no one despises his youth (4:12-16)?
ev: Recite or paraphrase 4:12
List the three things in 4:13

nodes.t: Honouring widows and caring for family
nodes.d: Timothy is to treat people of every age with respect, honour widows who are truly widows, expect families to care for their own, and set guidelines for enrolling widows and for younger widows.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who is to care for widows according to 5:4 and 5:16?
ev: State what 5:8 says about providing for one's own
Describe the tasks of a widow indeed (5:5, 5:10)

nodes.d: Elders who rule well are worthy of double honour; an accusation against an elder needs two or three witnesses; Timothy is to rebuke sin openly, act without partiality, and not lay hands hastily.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul says an accusation against an elder should be handled (5:19-21)?
ev: Say how 5:18 supports honouring elders
State the rule about accusations in 5:19

nodes.t: Servants, false gain, and godliness with contentment
nodes.d: Servants are to honour their masters; those who teach otherwise and suppose gain is godliness are to be avoided; godliness with contentment is great gain, and the love of money is a root of all evil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul says about godliness with contentment and the love of money (6:6-10)?
ev: Recite 6:6-8
Explain what 6:10 says about the love of money

nodes.t: Fight the good fight; charge to the rich
nodes.d: Timothy, a man of God, is to flee these things, pursue righteousness and godliness, fight the good fight of faith and keep the commandment until Christ's appearing; the rich are to trust the living God and do good.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul charges Timothy to do in 6:11-14?
ev: List what Timothy flees and follows (6:11)
State what the rich are told in 6:17-19

nodes.d: Deuteronomy records Moses' words to Israel on the plains of Moab in the fortieth year: a review of the journey, the ten commandments and the call to love the LORD, the laws for life in the land, the covenant renewal with its blessings and curses, Moses' song and blessing, and his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain where Israel is and what Moses is doing throughout Deuteronomy?
ev: Describe Deuteronomy as Moses' speeches before Israel enters the land and name its main parts.

nodes.t: Punishment limits, the ox and the brother's widow
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 25:1-12 limits a beating to forty stripes, forbids muzzling an ox that treads out the corn, gives the duty of a brother to raise up a name for a dead brother and the shoe-loosing ceremony if he refuses, and a rule about a wife seizing a man in a fight.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the purpose of the law of the brother's widow in 25:5-10?
ev: Say the limit on flogging and the reason (25:3).
Describe the duty of a living brother to a dead brother's childless widow.

nodes.d: Paul's first letter to the Thessalonian church, from thanksgiving for their faith (ch. 1) through his ministry and concern for them (2-3), to holy living, the Lord's coming and closing exhortations (4-5).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what 1 Thessalonians is about?
ev: Describe the movement: thanksgiving (1), ministry and Timothy (2-3), holy living and the Lord's coming (4-5)

nodes.t: Stir up the gift; do not be ashamed of the gospel
nodes.d: Paul remembers Timothy's sincere faith and tells him to stir up God's gift, not be ashamed of the testimony, and share in the afflictions of the gospel, since God saved and called us by his own purpose and grace and Christ brought life and immortality to light.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul tells Timothy to do in 1:6-8 and why (1:9-10)?
ev: Say whose faith dwelt in Timothy first (1:5)
Explain how 1:9-10 describes salvation

nodes.t: Elders in every city of Crete
nodes.d: Paul greets Titus, mentions the hope of eternal life promised before the world began, and tells him he left him in Crete to appoint elders who are blameless and hold fast the faithful word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul left Titus in Crete and what kind of men were to be elders (1:5-9)?
ev: State why Paul left Titus in Crete (1:5)
List some qualities of an elder in 1:6-9
